messages:
jamie_support: Customer reported SSE sessions closing early after ~10-30s. They see partial event stream, no JS error, network tab shows connection closed with 200 then FIN.

jamie_support: Repro steps they gave:
- Using client with Service Worker enabled and our hosted API endpoint
- Auth via Bearer token, streaming chat messages
- After a short time stream stops emitting; client tries reconnect but gets immediate closed responses from edge

jamie_support: I reproduced locally with a simple page + their SW. Curl reproducer that matches what they do:
```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=rlhf-chat\"
```
Result: initial 200 with event-stream content-type, then connection abruptly closes after a small chunk.

alex_frontend: Quick note — service workers will often serve a cached Response object which is non-streaming. If the SW does caches.match() and returns that Response, browser treats it as complete. That would cause immediate stream end (partial output).

alex_frontend: Paste of the problematic SW handler we saw in their repo:
```js
self.addEventListener('fetch', e => {
  e.respondWith(
    caches.match(e.request).then(cached => cached || fetch(e.request))
  )
})
```
This will hand a fully materialized Response to the page for SSE requests.

elaine_sre: Also saw edge logs where the CDN returns a 304 on conditional GET for the same SSE path when auth header stripped by some proxies — subsequent client-side request then gets a cached zero-length body. TL;DR: SW + cached SSE + CDN ETag/304 combo = truncated stream.

cdn_ops: Confirmed: our edge historically allows caching on some 200 responses if headers permit. For event-streams we need to ensure we never set ETag/Cache-Control that allows intermediate caches to store responses. On streamed endpoints we should return: Cache-Control: no-store, Pragma: no-cache, and avoid ETag/Last-Modified. Also set Vary: Authorization to avoid shared caches if auth is used.

jamie_support: Logs from customer (redacted):
```
GET /v1/streams 200 text/event-stream 12ms
GET /v1/streams 304 - 2ms (from edge-cache)
connection closed by client after 21s
```

jamie_support: They also had a service-worker update that started intercepting all requests a week ago. If they unregister the SW the stream is stable. So repro seems consistent.

alex_frontend: Suggested fixes for customers:
- In SW, detect SSE and bypass caches: if (e.request.headers.get('accept') === 'text/event-stream') return fetch(e.request)
- Or ensure caches.match() excludes streaming endpoints by URL pattern (e.g., /v1/streams)

elaine_sre: Platform fix items (internal):
- Ensure our streaming endpoints set Cache-Control: no-store and no ETag.
- Add Vary: Authorization when token-based auth is used.
- Update CDN rules to never cache responses with content-type text/event-stream.

cdn_ops: Can add a header rule that strips ETag from streaming responses at the edge and adds Cache-Control: no-store. I'll open a change ticket.

customer_ops: Temporary workaround we gave the customer: disable service worker or pin a client-side param to bypass SW; also recommended a websocket fallback until we roll platform change. They confirmed disabling SW works.

jamie_support: One extra gotcha — some polyfills/third-party libs try to emulate SSE by doing fetch + streaming parser. If they switched to a polyfill that uses cached responses, that will behave similarly. We asked them to check libs too.

elaine_sre: Follow-up tasks:
- Create infra ticket to update headers for /v1/streams (cdn-1023).
- Add a small doc snippet in devex about "Service Worker gotchas for EventSource" with code examples to bypass.
- Add an automated test that hits /v1/streams via our staging CDN and asserts no ETag/304 behavior.

alex_frontend: Quick patch for their SW to recommend:
```js
self.addEventListener('fetch', e => {
  if (e.request.headers.get('accept') === 'text/event-stream') {
    return e.respondWith(fetch(e.request))
  }
  // existing cache-first logic
})
```
jamie_support: I'll update the customer with repro, immediate mitigation (disable SW), and that we have infra change in progress. Thanks :thumbsup:

cdn_ops: Filed cdn-1023, assigning to edge-team. ETA for rollout to prod edges ~48h unless we hit config review.

elaine_sre: Adding note: if anyone hits auth refresh mid-stream (401s), the client may see the connection drop; separate ticket if we see auth refresh errors in logs. This thread is about truncation caused by caching/SW.

jamie_support: Closing loop — customer acknowledged workaround and will wait for edge change. I'll post follow-up after cdn-1023 deploy.
